title: Bead Rack

serves.summary: The learner shows numbers to 20 on a two-row bead rack in as few pushes as possible, using its groups of five and ten instead of counting by ones, and moves beads between rows to make a ten while keeping the total.

request.topic: Numbers to 20 on a bead rack, by fives and tens
request.objective: Show numbers to 20 on a two-row bead rack in as few pushes as possible by using its fives and tens, and make a ten from two rows without changing the total.

problems.ask: Show this number on the rack with one push.
problems.goal: The rack shows 7 beads on the left after one push: the top row's 5 red and 2 white slid over together.

problems.ask: Show this number on the rack with no more than two pushes.
problems.goal: The two rows together show 13 on the left, in at most two pushes (a full ten and 3, or any two-row split such as 5 and 8). The miss reads the digits: 1 on top and 3 below.

problems.ask: Make the top row a full ten, and keep the same number of beads on the left in all. Use no more than two pushes.
problems.goal: Top row 10 and bottom row 5 (still 15 in all), in at most two pushes: two beads go back on the bottom and two more slide over on top. The miss fills the top row and leaves the bottom alone, making 17.

problems.ask: Look at the card before it turns over. Then show the same number on your rack with no more than two pushes.
problems.goal: The card shows 7 on top and 6 below for 2.5 seconds, then turns over; the rack must show 13 in all in at most two pushes. The miss is one bead short on the bottom row (12), a miscount of the whites.
